ws.overviewHint: What this system is, how it works and what it can do now.
overview.claim: Fills the empty columns of an Excel table with values you can check.
overview.lead: You describe in your own words what you need. The AI proposes a plan built only from the steps listed below; you read it and approve it. Only then does the system run the plan, look the values up in open sources and write them into a copy of your table — together with where each value came from.
overview.how.table.title: Give it a table
overview.how.table.text: Upload an Excel workbook or open one of the examples.
overview.how.task.title: Say what to fill in
overview.how.task.text: Choose the columns to fill and describe the task in your own words — or ask the AI to suggest one.
overview.how.plan.title: Read the plan and approve it
overview.how.plan.text: The plan is shown step by step in plain words. Nothing runs before you approve it.
overview.how.result.title: Take the result
overview.how.result.text: Download the filled copy and the report. A name with several matches waits for your choice.
overview.canHint: A plan is built only from these steps. Where groups are shown, press one to show only it; open a card for details. The list comes from the server and grows together with the system.
overview.canHintAdvanced: A plan is built only from these steps. Where groups are shown, press one to show only it. Open a card for its contract exactly as the planning model is shown it, and the source that answers for it. The list is read from /api/capabilities.

overview.beginText: Begin with your own table, or see the whole path on a prepared example first.

overview.know.copy: Your file is not changed. The result is a copy, and a report says where each value came from.
overview.know.only: It does only what is listed here: it does not search the web freely and does not write texts.
overview.know.sends: When the AI builds a plan, your task and a sample of the table are sent to OpenAI; a run asks the listed sources about the names in the table.
overview.know.shared: This demo is one small server shared by everyone who has a code: one run at a time, and nothing is kept after a restart.
cap.geocode.title: Find a city and its coordinates and facts
cap.geocode.text: By the city's name and its country. If several places share the name, you choose. You can write the latitude, the longitude, the population or the timezone into columns; the source does not record every fact for every place.
cap.resolve_entity.title: Find a mountain by its name
cap.resolve_entity.text: By the mountain's name and its country, in an open knowledge base. If several mountains match, you choose.
cap.lookup_property.title: Read the elevation of a found mountain
cap.lookup_property.text: In metres, from the record of the mountain that was found.
cap.geodesic_distance.title: Calculate the straight-line distance between two places
cap.geodesic_distance.text: The shortest way over the Earth's surface between two found places, in kilometres.
cap.ratio.title: Compare two calculated values
cap.ratio.text: How many times one is larger than the other — for example, how much longer the road is than the straight line.
cap.road_distance.title: Calculate the driving distance by road

cat.web_search.title: AI web search
overview.web.off: Not switched on on this server. Whoever runs the server enables it with ENRICHMENT_ALLOW_WEB_LOOKUP; it also needs an OpenAI key.
overview.canHintWeb: The AI web search is not a step of a plan: you switch it on separately, under the task.
cap.geocode.needs: A city name and its country, from columns of the table. A state or region helps where a name is shared.
cap.geocode.gives: Coordinates (latitude and longitude), the population and the time zone, each into a column of its own. A value the source does not have stays empty.
cap.geocode.example: “Write the latitude, longitude and time zone of each city.”
cap.resolve_entity.needs: A mountain's name and its country, from columns of the table.
cap.resolve_entity.gives: The mountain's record in Wikidata, which later steps read from. If several mountains match, you choose.
cap.lookup_property.needs: A mountain that has already been found by its name.
cap.lookup_property.gives: Its elevation in metres, read from its record in Wikidata.
cap.lookup_property.example: “Write the elevation in metres of each mountain.”
cap.geodesic_distance.needs: Two places that earlier steps of the plan have found.
cap.geodesic_distance.gives: The straight-line distance between them in kilometres, calculated here.
cap.geodesic_distance.example: “Calculate the distance between the two cities in each row.”
cap.ratio.needs: Two values in the same unit, from the table or from earlier steps.
cap.ratio.gives: How many times the first is larger than the second, as a number without a unit.
cap.ratio.example: “How many times longer is the road than the straight line?”
cap.road_distance.needs: Two places that have been found. Offered only on a server that has an openrouteservice key.
cap.road_distance.gives: The length of a car route in kilometres, including ferries. It is computed by a routing service; there is no record to check it against.
cap.road_distance.example: “How far is it by road between the two cities?”
cap.web_lookup.needs: A task the listed sources cannot do, and the columns to fill. The values of the columns that identify a row go to OpenAI for every row. It stays off until you switch it on with the one switch under the task.
cap.web_lookup.gives: A value for each row, with the links it rests on. Not verified: nothing is checked against a record, and each row costs a model request.
cap.web_lookup.example: “Write the battery capacity in mAh of each phone model.”
mail.title: Build a table from e-mails
mail.hint: Choose .eml files, or one .zip of them. Each e-mail becomes one row of a table.
mail.privacy.where: The files are read by this application, on this computer. Nothing is sent to an AI model at this point. The names of your files stay in your browser.
mail.privacy.masked: In the table, the last digits of card numbers, phone numbers and your own e-mail address are replaced by a mask. Names and postal addresses are not masked.

extract.questionHint: Line breaks become spaces. The AI reads each e-mail with this question in mind and says when an e-mail is not about it.
extract.columnsHint: One value per column is read from each e-mail. The columns are added after the existing ones.

extract.need.question: Write what the e-mails are asked about.
extract.need.columns: Give every column a name that no other column has.
extract.trust.title: What to trust
extract.trust.rule: A value is kept only if the quote the AI gives for it is really in the e-mail. A number or a date is kept only if it can be read in that quote.
extract.trust.wording: Text, yes-or-no and choices may be the AI’s own wording of what the e-mail says. Every value comes with its quote, so that you can check it.
extract.notice.title: Before you build the plan
extract.notice.sends: When you run the plan, the text of every e-mail in the run is sent to OpenAI, one request per e-mail.
extract.notice.masked: Names and postal addresses in the e-mails are sent as they are; only card tails, phone numbers and your own address were masked.
extract.notice.cost: The requests cost tokens on the OpenAI key of this application. A long run can take several minutes.
extract.unavailable.loading: Checking what this server can do…
extract.unavailable.key: Reading values out of e-mails needs an OpenAI API key, and this application has none. Add one in the settings, or set OPENAI_API_KEY where the application is started and start it again.
extract.unavailable.network: Reading values out of e-mails needs the network switch of the application, and it is off. Start the application with --allow-network, or set ENRICHMENT_ALLOW_NETWORK=1.
extract.unavailable.other: Reading values out of e-mails is not available on this server. It needs an OpenAI API key and the network switch. The table is still shown above.
extract.rowsSetting: On a local installation the limit is set with ENRICHMENT_MAX_RUN_ROWS; restart the application after changing it.
extract.plan.title: Read values from the text of each e-mail
extract.plan.text: For each e-mail, an AI model reads its text and fills the columns below. A value is kept only if the passage it quotes is in the text.
